query: Eutectic high-entropy alloys contain dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries, where microcracking can initiate and lead to catastrophic damage during room-temperature tensile deformation. Conventional processing commonly raises strength at the expense of ductility, while the wide range of previously proposed microstructural-design and processing strategies has not eliminated room-temperature brittleness and limited tensile ductility. Under these constraints, what single intervention could improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility? State one testable hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts outcomes relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline, defines its boundary conditions, cites supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a hybrid-rolling process to eutectic high-entropy alloys will improve both strength and room-temperature tensile ductility by refining the lamellar colony structure and reducing internal boundaries, thereby inhibiting microcracking and enhancing the strength-ductility synergy.
generation.material_initial_state: Dual-phase lamellar colonies with numerous internal boundaries
generation.intervention: Hybrid-rolling process with a reduction ratio of 50% and a rolling temperature of 800°C
generation.structural_mediator: Refined lamellar colony structure with reduced internal boundaries
generation.mechanism: Thermo-mechanical processing-induced grain refinement and boundary modification, leading to improved strength-ductility synergy
generation.predicted_outcome: 25% increase in yield strength and 30% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline
generation.boundary: Hybrid-rolling process parameters: reduction ratio ≤ 70%, rolling temperature ≤ 900°C
generation.uncertainty: The exact mechanism of microcracking inhibition and the optimal hybrid-rolling process parameters are not well understood and require further investigation

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing of hybrid-rolled and unmodified eutectic high-entropy alloy samples at room temperature
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the hybrid-rolled samples exhibit less than 15% increase in yield strength or less than 20% increase in tensile ductility relative to the unmodified baseline, the hypothesis is falsified
